items.excerpt: Generative AI has made language tools ubiquitous for multilingual researchers, but it introduces risks of homogenized texts and semantic slippage — and suspicion from journals either way.
Researchers developed Apollo, a large language model that fills in the gaps in damaged ancient Greek papyrus fragments to help read and translate tattered historical texts.

A Stanford team's Nature paper introduces Paper2Agent, an automated framework that converts research papers into interactive AI agents, turning static publications into active systems readers can query.
For Peer Review Week 2026 the Chefs name uncomfortable truths about review capacity, with AI writing assistants swelling submissions and reviewers quietly using AI despite few journal policies.
A guest post argues scholarly publishing debates AI governance on stage while staff quietly use AI to get work done, and asks what incentive structures keep the industry from adapting.
Audio and AI lead Frankfurt 2026's program, including an 'AI Narration Beyond the Lab' debate with Storytel, Blinkist and Hörbuch Hamburg on where synthetic narration works and listener acceptance.
Agents heading to Frankfurt expect AI to hover over the rights center after high-profile cancellations of novels suspected of being AI-generated, with greater scrutiny of provenance and authorship.

At BISG's 50th-anniversary forum, executives including Rakuten Kobo discussed how AI-driven data checking and cleaning could fix book metadata and whether publishers should feed retailers data AI can consume.
Oxford University Press updated author and editor guidelines with a policy on what AI use must be disclosed in manuscripts, alongside a survey of 2,600+ researchers on AI disclosure.
Clarivate's Pulse of the Library 2026 finds a widening gap between libraries actively implementing AI and those still experimenting; 16% globally report moderate-to-active AI implementation.
